3. The respondent No.1 . Commissioner of Customs, Excise and VAT has entered appearance and contested the Rule by tiling affidavit-in-opposition contending that the petitioner is liable to pay the demand made in the impugned order dated 7.1.2003 by way of VAT as a trader of the imported sugar in terms of the Notification vide SRO No.143/Ain/201/308 issued under section 5(2) of the VAT Ain,1991 and the Rule issued is thus liable to be rejected. 

 8. Section 5(1) of the VAT Act deals with the determination of the price of the imported commodities for the purpose of imposition of VAT. Section 5(2) deals with the determination of price of the commodities other than the imported ones for the purpose of imposition and payment of VAT by the manufacturers, producers and traders. Second proviso to section 5(2) empowers the National Board of Revenue (NBR) to determine the rate or quantum of the value to be added for the purpose of fixation of the value of any goods or commodity other than the imported ones for the purpose of payment of VAT thereon by the manufacturers, producers or traders. SRO 143 dated 7th June, 2001, Annexure-1 to the affidavit-in-opposition has been issued by the NBR under the second proviso to section 5(2) for determination of the value of the goods which is not imported for the purpose of realization of VAT. The said SRO 143 dated 7th June, 2001 has therefore no relevance or application to the goods in question, namely the sugar imported by the petitioner on which VAT was paid as assessed under section 5(1) at the stage of its import. If the impugned order of demand dated 7.1.2003 is taken to be issued pursuant to the said SRO 143 dated 7th June, 2001, as it is claimed, it is in violation of sections 3(3) and 5(2) of the VAT Act.
